audit_type: Targeted primary-source bibliography and claim-attribution audit; not a systematic review or novelty certificate
scope: Historical full symmetric-group QFT constructions, the induction framework, coherent preparation and amplification, finite-precision compilation, and nearby character-transform results.
ai_assistance: This audit was prepared with AI-assisted public bibliographic searches and targeted source reading. No unpublished manuscript was uploaded and no human-read certification is implied.

verification_policy.evidence: Primary papers, publisher records, arXiv author records, and author/institutional publication records. Search snippets were used for metadata only when direct publisher access failed.
verification_policy.read_scope: Per-source fields distinguish targeted full-text passages from metadata/abstract-only checks. No source is represented as read in its entirety.
verification_policy.peer_review: Venue status is distinguished from mathematical correctness. No comprehensive retraction, conflict-of-interest, author-background, or venue-index audit was performed.
verification_policy.bibliographic_apis: No Semantic Scholar or Crossref API verification was used; direct primary-source checks were used instead. DOI resolution failures are recorded, not treated as nonexistent references.
verification_policy.field: Mathematical/theoretical-computer-science evidence; clinical evidence hierarchies and statistical risk-of-bias grades are inapplicable.

bibliography.title: Quantum Fourier transform for the symmetric group

sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no journal status inferred
sources.read_scope: Theorems 1.1--1.2; Lemma 2.4; Definition 3.6, Lemma 3.7, Theorem 3.8; Section 4.1; Section 5.5 discussion; Section 6 precision discussion; Appendices A.2.1 and A.3.1.
verified_claims: Theorem 1.1: full QFT uses soft-O(n^3) one-/two-qubit gates and soft-O(n^(3/2)) qubits; inverse diamond-error dependence is polylogarithmic.
Theorem 1.2 reanalyzes the Kawano--Sekigawa route as soft-O(n^(7/2)) gates. Section 5.5 charges coherent Givens-angle computation.
Branching ratios, induction identity, near-linear successor preparation, and sorting-network corner extraction are inherited ingredients.
supports: Primary normalized full-QFT baseline and representation-theoretic formulas
limitations: Theorem 1.1 states soft-O(n^(3/2)) qubits, but its Section 6 proof and Appendix A.2.1 suggest near-linear workspace for the Beals route. Do not claim a strict space improvement without reconciling this discrepancy.
Coherent arithmetic and sorting are inherited.
Its primitive count is one-/two-qubit gates, not a Clifford+T table.

sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no journal status inferred
sources.read_scope: Metadata, Section 3.3/Theorem 3.5, and Section 4/Lemma 4.1/Theorem 4.2 statements and surrounding definitions.
verified_claims: Theorem 3.5 composes induction transforms along multiplicity-free subgroup chains into a QFT in a Gelfand--Tsetlin basis.
Theorem 4.2 presents Beals' ordered transversal-accumulation construction.
supports: General framework and attribution for the induction recurrence and conventional assembly

No new full-S_n subcubic bound was identified in the inspected portions. The whole paper was not audited here.

sources.publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal review; publisher table of contents verifies metadata/DOI
sources.read_scope: Section 3 pseudocode, recurrences (1)--(9), and following finite-precision caveat.
verified_claims: Sequence length scales as log(1/epsilon)^(log(5)/log(3/2)); pointer-based arithmetic runtime has exponent log(3)/log(3/2).

bibliography.title: Time-Space Efficient Simulations of Quantum Computations

sources.publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article; publisher metadata verified
sources.read_scope: Theorem 4.5 and its surrounding explanation, printed pp.32--33; finite-precision/output-mode discussion and Algorithm 1 in Section 4.3.3, pp.39--40.
verified_claims: For fixed dimension and an adjoint-closed finite SU(d) net, Theorem 4.5 gives phase-sensitive epsilon-approximation in deterministic polylog(1/epsilon) time and O(log(1/epsilon)) space from polynomially accurate input matrices.
limitations: The theorem does not certify the repository's floating-point compiler.
A concrete Clifford+T application must justify phase normalization and controlled-gate construction; bare projective approximation is insufficient.

bibliography.title: An efficient Hamiltonian-based quantum algorithm for characters of the symmetric group

sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no journal status inferred
sources.read_scope: Character-transform definition, Theorems 1.3--1.4, and Section 5.1 resource/error construction, especially Theorem 5.1 and equations (5.30)--(5.33).
verified_claims: Theorem 5.1 gives a coherent character transform on valid cycle-type labels with clean-input operator-norm error delta, soft-O(n^(5/2)) gates at inverse-polynomial delta, and O(n) qubits.
The algorithm uses coherent character-state preparation and amplified spectral erasure; it is not the full n!-dimensional group QFT.
supports: Nearby subcubic symmetric-group transform and essential scope distinction
limitations: The inspected statement is a one-/two-qubit gate/QSVT resource claim, not a reported Clifford+T bit-compilation theorem.
Do not conflate rigorous QSVT bounds with the paper's separate leading-order state-dependent Trotter estimates.

sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no journal status inferred
sources.read_scope: Section II.1/Theorem II.1 and Section IV restriction algorithm, resource discussion, and comparison to Rathore--Zhou.
verified_claims: Theorem II.1 identifies the character transform with the group Fourier transform restricted to the group-algebra center. Section IV removes matrix-index registers coherently using controlled generalized Bell-state unpreparation.
supports: Why a character transform on conjugacy-class data is not the full QFT
limitations: Restriction overhead depends on coherent access to representation dimensions and preparations; no automatic sharp finite-gate exponent for our application is inferred.
